capabilities.title: Visual Studio Code

capabilities.title: Git for Windows

instructions: Install Git, keep the recommended beginner defaults, then configure your name and email.

capabilities.title: GitHub account

weeks.title: Compile, Run, and Values
weeks.outcome: Build, debug, explain, and verify a console receipt calculator.

study.objective: Learn and actively rehearse compiler, main, iostream, type, namespace qualifier so you can explain, select, debug, and apply them while creating a console receipt calculator.

resources.purpose: Learn the exact definitions, applications, and mistakes assessed by the Week 1 Skill Check, then preview the a console receipt calculator contract.
Rehearse the same five weekly concepts through prediction, error recognition, and explanation without affecting progression.

skillCheck.title: Compile, Run, and Values Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 1 guide defines compiler. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: translates C++ source into a program
a set of values and operations

questions.explanation: compiler means translates C++ source into a program; it is used to run g++ main.cpp -o app. Avoid this mistake: expect an IDE to replace compiler understanding.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to run g++ main.cpp -o app. Which concept from the Week 1 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: compiler is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect an IDE to replace compiler understanding.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for main, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: expect cout to format every value automatically for the learner
add using namespace std everywhere without understanding collisions

questions.explanation: main means the program entry function; it is used to return 0 from main. Avoid this mistake: put statements at namespace scope.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to put statements at namespace scope. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: main is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to put statements at namespace scope.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 1 guide correctly demonstrates iostream?
questions.explanation: iostream means stream input and output facilities; it is used to use std::cout. Avoid this mistake: expect cout to format every value automatically for the learner.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: use std::cout?
questions.explanation: iostream is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect cout to format every value automatically for the learner.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain type before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: a set of values and operations
selects a name from a namespace
translates C++ source into a program

questions.explanation: type means a set of values and operations; it is used to use double for measured values. Avoid this mistake: mix types without considering conversion.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "a set of values and operations". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: type is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to mix types without considering conversion.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that namespace qualifier was misunderstood?

options.label: expect an IDE to replace compiler understanding
expect cout to format every value automatically for the learner
add using namespace std everywhere without understanding collisions

questions.explanation: namespace qualifier means selects a name from a namespace; it is used to write std::string. Avoid this mistake: add using namespace std everywhere without understanding collisions.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—add using namespace std everywhere without understanding collisions—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: namespace qualifier is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to add using namespace std everywhere without understanding collisions.

builds.title: Microbuild: a console receipt calculator
builds.outcome: A working, tested a console receipt calculator.
builds.brief: Deliverable: a console receipt calculator. Required behavior: demonstrate compiler, main, iostream, type, namespace qualifier; complete one normal, one boundary, and one invalid case; and keep a short expected-versus-actual test record. Evidence: the exact run command, the repaired defect, the three final results, and an honest README.

steps.text: Write a three-case contract for a console receipt calculator: one normal case, one boundary case, and one invalid case. For each, record the input or action and the expected result before coding.
Create the runnable source and implement the normal case first. Make compiler, main, iostream visible in the code or interface, then run the exact launch command once.

Add the boundary and invalid-case behavior using type and namespace qualifier. Deliberately reproduce this weekly mistake—add using namespace std everywhere without understanding collisions—record the symptom, repair one cause, and rerun the same case.
Run all three contract cases again. In README, record the environment, exact run command, expected versus actual results, repaired defect, and one known limit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A learner can follow the README command and run a console receipt calculator through its stated normal case without an unexplained error.
The finished work visibly demonstrates the Week 1 concepts: compiler, main, iostream, type, namespace qualifier.
The test record lists normal, boundary, and invalid inputs or actions with both expected and actual results.
The debugging note names the failing case, observed symptom, root cause, single repair, successful rerun, and one known limit.

hints: If the normal case fails, reduce it to the smallest input or action involving compiler and inspect the observed value before editing.
If the boundary or invalid case fails, revisit the guide warning "add using namespace std everywhere without understanding collisions" and change one cause at a time.

skillCheck.title: Input and Control Flow Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 2 guide defines cin state. Which description matches that definition?
questions.explanation: cin state means whether formatted input succeeded; it is used to test if (std::cin >> age). Avoid this mistake: use a failed stream repeatedly without clearing it.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to test if (std::cin >> age). Which concept from the Week 2 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: cin state is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use a failed stream repeatedly without clearing it.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for if statement, which warning identifies the error to avoid?
questions.explanation: if statement means conditional execution; it is used to choose a fare from age. Avoid this mistake: use = instead of ==.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to use = instead of ==. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: if statement is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use = instead of ==.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 2 guide correctly demonstrates switch?
questions.explanation: switch means selection by integral-like cases; it is used to handle menu commands. Avoid this mistake: use duplicate case labels.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: handle menu commands?
questions.explanation: switch is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use duplicate case labels.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain logical operator before coding. Which explanation is accurate?
questions.explanation: logical operator means combines conditions; it is used to check age >= 0 && age <= 120. Avoid this mistake: confuse && with bitwise &.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "combines conditions". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: logical operator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to confuse && with bitwise &.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that scope block was misunderstood?

options.label: use a failed stream repeatedly without clearing it

questions.explanation: scope block means a region delimited by braces; it is used to keep temporary choice local. Avoid this mistake: expect a block local later.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—expect a block local later—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: scope block is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect a block local later.

questions.prompt: The Week 3 guide defines for loop. Which description matches that definition?
questions.explanation: for loop means counted repetition; it is used to process a fixed number of scores. Avoid this mistake: write a non-terminating update.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to process a fixed number of scores. Which concept from the Week 3 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: for loop is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to write a non-terminating update.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for range-for, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: modify copies when references are required
print when a caller needs the value

questions.explanation: range-for means iteration over container elements; it is used to visit each vector value. Avoid this mistake: modify copies when references are required.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to modify copies when references are required. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: range-for is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to modify copies when references are required.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 3 guide correctly demonstrates function?

options.label: process a fixed number of scores

questions.explanation: function means named reusable behavior; it is used to write calculateAverage. Avoid this mistake: duplicate logic in main.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: write calculateAverage?
questions.explanation: function is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to duplicate logic in main.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain parameter before coding. Which explanation is accurate?
questions.explanation: parameter means a function input declaration; it is used to accept const vector reference. Avoid this mistake: copy large containers without reason.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "a function input declaration". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: parameter is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to copy large containers without reason.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that return value was misunderstood?

options.label: print when a caller needs the value

questions.explanation: return value means a result delivered to caller; it is used to return an average. Avoid this mistake: print when a caller needs the value.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—print when a caller needs the value—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: return value is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to print when a caller needs the value.

skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 4 guide defines std::string. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: references becoming unusable after container change

questions.explanation: std::string means a managed text value; it is used to store a full learner name. Avoid this mistake: treat it as a raw null-terminated buffer.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to store a full learner name. Which concept from the Week 4 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: std::string is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to treat it as a raw null-terminated buffer.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for std::vector, which warning identifies the error to avoid?
questions.explanation: std::vector means a resizable sequence; it is used to push_back new scores. Avoid this mistake: index past size.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to index past size. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: std::vector is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to index past size.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 4 guide correctly demonstrates size?
